title: How Much Protein Do Women Need to Lose Fat?
intro: A general guide many people use is an estimated 1.2-1.6 g of protein per kg of body weight per day, so a 60 kg woman needs roughly 70-95 g. The easiest way: include a protein source at every meal, about 20-30 g.

sections.h: Why protein matters when losing fat
sections.p: Protein helps you feel full longer, so you get fewer afternoon cravings. It also helps keep your muscle while you're eating a little less than usual. If your weight is much higher than your target, calculate using your target weight so the number is more realistic.

These are rough estimates for typical Malaysian portions. One egg: about 6 g. Palm-sized chicken: about 20-25 g. One medium ikan kembung: about 20 g. 100 g tempe: about 18 g. One piece of tofu: about 8-10 g. One glass of milk: about 8 g.

sections.h: At the mamak and nasi campur shop
sections.p: At the mamak, choose roti telur over roti kosong, or add a half-boiled egg. Ayam tandoori or ayam bakar are also good choices. At the nasi campur shop, take one clear protein dish like fish, chicken or egg. Add tofu or dhal if you want more.

Boil eggs for 3-4 days at once and bring them to the office. Cook extra chicken or fish at dinner and use it for the next day's packed lunch. For snacks, try unsweetened yogurt, milk or nuts in small portions. This reduces how much you rely on meeting kuih.
If you have kidney disease, are pregnant or have certain health conditions, ask your doctor first before adding a lot more protein. For most healthy women, protein from normal food is enough.

action: Record what you eat for 2 days and work out your estimated daily protein.
Boil 6-8 eggs on Sunday for breakfast or snacks this week.
Make sure every lunch has one palm-sized protein dish.
At the mamak, swap roti kosong for roti telur or add one egg.
Add tofu, tempe or dhal to at least 3 meals this week.
myth: Many women are afraid that eating more protein will make their body 'bulky like a man'. Actually, building big muscles needs specific training and a long time, and enough protein usually just helps your body look more toned.

faq.q: Do I need to weigh all my food?
faq.a: No need. Use your palm as a guide, which is one palm of protein for every meal. Weigh only once in a while if you want to check your estimates.

faq.q: If I don't eat meat, can I still get enough protein?
faq.a: Yes. Eggs, milk, yogurt, tofu, tempe, dhal and beans are all protein sources. Combine a few sources every day so it's easier to reach your target.

faq.q: Will more protein make my weight drop straight away?
faq.a: Protein isn't a magic switch. It helps you feel full and protects your muscle, but fat loss still depends on your total calories, movement and consistency.
